About the Surgical Technologist event

Surgical Technologist is a Health Professions event in the HOSA secondary division. Format: testing · skills.

Ten in-depth lessons following the HOSA Surgical Technologist 2026–27 test plan (instrumentation 30%, asepsis and sterility 20%, surgical anatomy 20%, profession, environment and hemostasis/wound closure 10% each) and all six Round Two skills: instrument identification, surgical scrub, open gloving, gowning and closed gloving, passing instruments and loading and passing sutures. Built around the AST’s Surgical Technology for the Surgical Technologist and Nemitz’s Surgical Instrumentation, with instrument matching and spelling drills, sterile-field rules, sterilization indicators, suture and needle sorting, labeled anatomy diagrams and step-ordering for every rating sheet. Always follow the scenario and rating sheets you are given.

Surgical Technologist lessons

Unit 1 · The profession and the OR environment

Test plan: profession 10%, physical environment and safety 10%.

  1. The surgical technologist profession and the event 25 min

  2. The operating room environment and safety standards 30 min

    An operating room is designed to fight infection: filtered air pushes contaminants out, traffic is controlled and temperature and humidity are kept in narrow ranges. It is also full of hazards—electrosurgical units…

Unit 2 · Asepsis, sterilization and sterile attire

Test plan: surgical asepsis and sterility 20%. Skills II, III and IV.

  1. Surgical asepsis and the surgical scrub (Skill II) 30 min

    Surgical site infections are among the most common infections acquired in hospitals, and every one starts with microorganisms reaching the wound. Surgical asepsis—the rules that keep the sterile field free of…

  2. Decontamination, sterilization and open gloving (Skill III) 30 min

    A tray of instruments used on one patient may be used on another just hours later. Between those cases, the instruments are cleaned, inspected, packaged and sterilized—and every step must be done correctly, or the next…

  3. Gowning and gloving, the sterile field and draping (Skill IV) 30 min

    After the scrub, the CST must put on a sterile gown and gloves without touching anything non-sterile—using only the inside of the gown and the gown’s cuffs. Then comes setting up the back table and Mayo stand, gowning…

Unit 3 · Instruments and wound closure

Test plan: instrumentation 30%, hemostasis and wound closure 10%. Skills I, V and VI.

  1. Instruments I: parts, classification, cutting and grasping instruments (Skill I) 30 min

    A general surgery tray can hold more than 100 instruments, and many look alike. A Crile and a Kelly differ only in where the serrations stop; an Adson and a Brown-Adson differ in their teeth. In Skill I you see 15…

  2. Instruments II: clamps, retractors, equipment and passing (Skills I and V) 30 min

    The surgeon holds out a hand without looking up—and the right clamp, closed and pointed the right way, lands in the palm with a gentle snap. Passing instruments well means knowing the instruments, the surgeon’s hand…

  3. Hemostasis, wound healing and wound closure (Skill VI) 30 min

    Every incision cuts blood vessels and every operation ends with closing a wound. Controlling bleeding, choosing the right suture and needle and understanding how wounds heal determine whether the patient recovers…

Unit 4 · Surgical anatomy and patient care

Test plan: surgical anatomy and physiology 20%.

  1. Surgical anatomy I: abdominal wall, digestive and genitourinary systems 35 min

    To pass the right instrument at the right moment, a surgical technologist must know what the surgeon is cutting through and what lies beneath. Every layer of the abdominal wall, every organ and every capsule has a name…

  2. Surgical anatomy II and patient care: cardiovascular, orthopedic, neuro and anesthesia 30 min

    Surgical technologists scrub for everything from a hip replacement to open-heart surgery to brain tumor removal. Each specialty has its own anatomy, instruments and risks, and every patient goes through anesthesia…

Sample Surgical Technologist questions

1. An indirect inguinal hernia passes through which opening?

  1. The femoral canal
  2. The deep inguinal ring
  3. The umbilicus
  4. The esophageal hiatus
Show answer

B. The deep inguinal ring

Indirect hernias follow the inguinal canal through the deep ring. Direct hernias push through a weak area of the posterior wall (Hesselbach’s triangle).

2. When does the surgical “time-out” take place?

  1. During closing counts
  2. After the patient leaves the OR
  3. Immediately before the incision
  4. When the patient is admitted
Show answer

C. Immediately before the incision

During the time-out, the team confirms the correct patient, procedure and site before incision, as part of the Universal Protocol.

3. What three elements make up the fire triangle in surgery?

  1. Water, heat and pressure
  2. Oxygen, carbon dioxide and nitrogen
  3. Light, sound and motion
  4. Oxygen, fuel and an ignition source
Show answer

D. Oxygen, fuel and an ignition source

In the OR, oxidizers include oxygen and nitrous oxide, fuels include drapes and alcohol preps, and ignition sources include electrosurgery and lasers.
